functions.label: Shared one-rank update primitives
functions.evidence_summary: The common up/down hook 0x00B498D0 / 0x00B498F0 calls these to increment/decrement the instance field at +0x50, then refresh the level-indexed value at +0x4C through 0x0046FA80. The exact-build vtables for Immolation (0x00F277EC), Carrion Swarm (0x00F887B0), Shadow Strike (0x00F98714), and Cluster Rockets (0x00FB2C6C) point directly to these common hooks at +0x2E4 / +0x2E8. Earthquake (0x00F85CF0) uses wrappers 0x00C298D0 / 0x00C298F0, which call the common hooks and then an additional virtual slot +0x434. This is a high-value shared rank lifecycle with a visible class-specific extension point.
functions.related_addresses_semantics: Addresses mentioned in the source evidence; not a verified caller/callee edge list.

functions.label: Shared attached-ability disable/enable state transitions
functions.evidence_summary: Disable increments the ability instance counter at +0x3C; the first transition from zero invokes virtual +0xE0, clears instance flag bit 0x2, and invokes +0xC4. Enable decrements the same counter; a transition from positive to below one invokes +0xE4 and may restore flag bit 0x2 plus invoke +0xC8, depending on unit flag +0x164 & 4. Both paths refresh shared UI state. A secondary instance counter at +0x40 is also adjusted based on the wrapper's hideUI argument. Full-analysis Ghidra found 107 direct callers of disable and 99 of enable. In sampled exact-build vtables, Carrion Swarm (0x00F887B0), Shadow Strike (0x00F98714), and Cluster Rockets (0x00FB2C6C) use defaults at these hooks: +0xC4=0x0046A470, +0xC8=0x0046A480, +0xE0=0x0046A4A0, +0xE4=0x0046A500. Immolation (0x00F277EC) overrides +0xC4=0x00B6D6D0 and +0xE4=0x00B6D6F0; Earthquake (0x00F85CF0) overrides +0xC4=0x00C29CB0 and +0xC8=0x00C29CD0. The counters can be adjusted without a transition, so inspect callers and class hooks before assigning exact gameplay meaning to every branch.
functions.related_addresses_semantics: Addresses mentioned in the source evidence; not a verified caller/callee edge list.

functions.label: JASS GetUnitAbilityLevel / SetUnitAbilityLevel wrappers
functions.evidence_summary: All four level natives share a preflight check for internal tag 0x2B61676C and object field +0x20 == 0; the meaning of this gate is not yet named. They then locate the attached instance through 0x006D6570. Get returns its stored zero-based rank at object offset +0x50, plus one, or zero if no eligible instance is found. Set clamps the requested level to [1, maxLevel] using 0x0046F5C0, then repeatedly invokes virtual +0x2E4 to raise or +0x2E8 to lower rank on that same instance. It does not remove/recreate the ability. IncUnitAbilityLevel (0x00498B20) and DecUnitAbilityLevel (0x0048F150) use the same virtual hooks with max/level-one bounds.
functions.related_addresses_semantics: Addresses mentioned in the source evidence; not a verified caller/callee edge list.

functions.label: JASS UnitAddAbility / UnitRemoveAbility wrappers
functions.evidence_summary: Registered in the native table at 0x0049B3C0. Add resolves the unit, looks up the requested rawcode and returns false if an instance already exists, then calls factory 0x00AF3BA0 inside synchronization helpers and returns whether it created an instance. Remove resolves the unit, looks up the rawcode, removes the found instance through 0x006D8530, and returns whether it found one. Both notify through 0x005F6D00 after a successful change. These named natives provide a direct, reproducible path into shared ability ownership and teardown.
functions.related_addresses_semantics: Addresses mentioned in the source evidence; not a verified caller/callee edge list.

functions.label: JASS UnitDamageTarget damage-event handoff
functions.evidence_summary: Exact-build disassembly confirms the wrapper resolves source unit and target widget handles, validates attack-type, damage-type, and weapon-type indices, initializes a stack payload through 0x006A9940, then calls the target's +0x120 virtual method and returns true after dispatch. Carrion Swarm independently initializes the same payload and dispatches through the same slot. For CUnit targets that slot resolves to 0x006677C0, which performs unit-specific mitigation and life mutation. This establishes shared payload/receiver infrastructure for JASS damage and Carrion Swarm, not the ordinary attack-hit caller.
functions.related_addresses_semantics: Addresses mentioned in the source evidence; not a verified caller/callee edge list.

functions.label: JASS UnitMakeAbilityPermanent wrapper
functions.evidence_summary: Resolves the unit, finds the attached instance by rawcode through 0x006D6570, then increments or decrements the integer field at instance offset +0x38 according to permanent. It returns whether an instance was found. This field is separate from disable counters +0x3C / +0x40; its downstream persistence/removal effect is not yet traced.

functions.label: Configured damage-bonus matrix lookup
functions.evidence_summary: Lazily loads seven eight-entry rows named DamageBonusSpells, DamageBonusNormal, DamageBonusPierce, DamageBonusSiege, DamageBonusMagic, DamageBonusChaos, and DamageBonusHero. It returns the matrix entry at param3 + param2 * 8; the CUnit damage receiver calls it with values derived from event payload offset +0x20 and unit offset +0x1EC (or constant 4 on one branch). Row names are established from configuration-string reads, but the two index enums and exact column meanings are not yet mapped. Ethereal adjustments are read separately through EtherealDamageBonus and allied-ethereal logic.

functions.label: General spell target validation
functions.evidence_summary: Exact-build disassembly shows two common target-state rejection predicates run first. If both return zero, the helper walks a global linked registry (iterator accessor 0x007FC7E0), invokes each registered validator's vtable slot +0x26C with the candidate and context, and stops at the first nonzero return. Phoenix Fire's candidate callback at 0x00C0F1E0 is one verified caller; Ghidra analysis found 64 direct call references from 64 functions. Returns are internal validation results, not damage or a general order-acceptance boolean. Predicate meanings and runtime registry membership remain unresolved.

functions.evidence_summary: The body registers an instance, caches selected special rawcodes on the unit, invokes virtual lifecycle hooks on the new instance, and notifies already attached instances. Full-analysis Ghidra found 54 direct calls from 34 caller functions. This is a useful point to verify whether an ability's resulting status object actually becomes attached and enters shared unit lifecycle dispatch; it does not itself prove the ability-specific creation rules or expiry behavior.

Full-analysis Ghidra found 20 direct calls from 20 functions. This could help trace shared state changes or cleanup, but the affected state and virtual operations are not semantically identified yet. Treat it as a call-chain waypoint, not a verified ability contract.

functions.label: Buff-object creation path used by UnitApplyTimedLife
functions.evidence_summary: The JASS native wrapper at 0x004AED50 resolves the unit and passes the requested buff code and duration here. This routine selects a buff prototype/factory, initializes the created object through virtual slot +0x324, attaches it through 0x006D4560, then runs a post-attach helper. Its only direct caller found is the UnitApplyTimedLife wrapper, so this is a confirmed native path, not yet a shared spell-cast helper. The default branch selects BTLF via 0x006F4C40.

functions.label: JASS BlzUnitDisableAbility bridge
functions.evidence_summary: This is the only disable-by-rawcode native name found in the pinned executable; no UnitDisableAbility registration/string was found. The wrapper resolves the unit and passes ability rawcode, hideUI, and flag to this helper. The helper finds the existing attached instance through 0x006D6570, then routes to disable or enable counters. On enable it passes hideUI == false to the inverse counter path, so preserve the wrapper's argument mapping when evaluating UI behavior. The helper has one direct caller: the JASS wrapper.

functions.label: Attached ability/status instance lookup by rawcode
functions.evidence_summary: Function-body inspection shows fast paths for several fixed FOURCCs, then iteration over attached instances and comparison through their rawcode getter. Phoenix Fire queries Bpxf and rejects a candidate when the status instance is already present. Full-analysis Ghidra found 959 direct call references from 681 caller functions, making this the strongest high-reuse starting point. The lookup does not establish application, refresh, expiry, or dispel behavior.

functions.label: Attached ability/status instance removal
functions.evidence_summary: The body marks the instance as removed, notifies sibling attached objects through a virtual hook, unlinks it from the owner's attached-instance list, refreshes list metadata, and clears cached pointers for selected rawcodes. Full-analysis Ghidra found 221 direct calls from 174 functions. This is a strong shared path for tracing dispel, expiry, death cleanup, or ability removal, but caller and virtual-hook analysis is still needed to identify which cause initiated each removal.

functions.label: Shared JASS buff-filter and attached-instance removal loop
functions.evidence_summary: Both UnitRemoveBuffs (0x004AF5E0) and UnitRemoveBuffsEx (0x004AF610) resolve the unit and call this function. The extended wrapper reorders its category arguments into the helper's internal order; the simple wrapper supplies a fixed set of category switches. The helper walks attached instances, checks positive/negative and category predicates through virtual slots, and calls 0x006D8530 on matches. It fetches the next list entry before removal and returns a removal count internally. Full-analysis Ghidra found 27 direct calls from 22 functions. For the BTLF object created by UnitApplyTimedLife, vtable slots +0x1E0 and +0x1E4 point to 0x0046A9A0 and 0x0046A9C0; both methods return zero. These are the two polarity predicates the loop requires when removeNegative or removePositive is enabled. Static flow therefore excludes this BTLF instance from both native removal calls, independent of the other category switches. Verify the concrete instance class before applying that conclusion to another timed status.
functions.related_addresses_semantics: Addresses mentioned in the source evidence; not a verified caller/callee edge list.

The callback is referenced by many class vtables, so it is a shared lifecycle primitive. The event's semantic name and whether a particular caller uses it for expiry remain unresolved.

functions.label: AbilityData-driven ability instance factory
functions.evidence_summary: UnitAddAbility reaches this after rejecting an existing instance with 0x006D6570. The factory resolves the AbilityData row, dispatches on its implementation code at row offset +0x30 to concrete class constructors, initializes the instance through virtual slot +0x80 with the owner and data at row offset +0x18, then attaches through 0x006D4560. Full-analysis Ghidra found 10 direct calls from 10 functions. This is a strong route for connecting named JASS add/remove calls to class-specific constructors; the factory's large implementation-code switch is not itself proof of a class's runtime behavior.

functions.label: Pocket Factory summon missile setup and impact
functions.evidence_summary: CAbilitySummonFactory callback 0x00C82310 resolves the MNsy missile row and dispatches virtual slot +0xD4; the pinned CMissileSummonFactory vtable 0x00FB48A0 maps setup to 0x00C828A0. functions.evidence_summary: Spirit Wolf passes its resolved summon code, owner, and placement through this wrapper; it validates the unit row and delegates construction to 0x00687CA0 with creation flags. It has 15 direct references. Serpent Ward bypasses this wrapper and calls 0x00687CA0 directly. Do not assume all summons use the wrapper just because the constructor is shared.

functions.label: Generic widget route 0x006BD260 / base value method 0x00664A60
functions.evidence_summary: CWidget +0x120 calls 0x006C0100, negates the input value, then dispatches through +0x128. The base CWidget +0x128 implementation writes zero to the output. Subclasses can override these methods; a successful UnitDamageTarget return only proves dispatch occurred.

functions.label: Unit damage receiver 0x006677C0 / value-change method 0x00668DB0
functions.evidence_summary: The CUnit constructor installs vtable 0x00E9C504. Its +0x120 method returns early when unit flag +0x164 has bit 0x100; checks MagicImmunesResistDamage and payload-class predicates; dispatches attached-object callbacks through slots +0xF8, +0xFC, and +0x100; reads configured DamageBonusSpells/Normal/Pierce/Siege/Magic/Chaos/Hero values through 0x0067B920; and applies configured ethereal adjustments. In its first attached-object pass, it invokes +0xFC only when that object's +0xF8 returns 1; other nonzero return values are collected for later callback phases. It calls 0x006A0630, computes an adjusted amount, then invokes its own +0x128 method (0x00668DB0) with the negative amount and returns the resulting value through an output pointer. The independently inspected UnitDamageTarget and Carrion Swarm call sites both dispatch through +0x120, establishing shared unit-specific mitigation/value-change infrastructure for those paths. Which attached-object groups correspond to ordinary attack-hit processing remains unresolved.
functions.related_addresses_semantics: Addresses mentioned in the source evidence; not a verified caller/callee edge list.

functions.label: Destructable route 0x006CE850 / value method 0x006CEF00
functions.evidence_summary: The destructable override delegates value change through the CWidget route, which virtually calls destructable +0x128, then checks the resulting destroyed state and enters an effect/lifecycle path. +0x128 updates the destructable's stored life value and calls 0x006D10C0 on a threshold transition. This is a separate route from the CUnit mitigation routine.
functions.related_addresses_semantics: Addresses mentioned in the source evidence; not a verified caller/callee edge list.

functions.label: Damage group 2: +0xF8=0x00C20940, +0xFC=0x00C20950, +0x364=0x00C20AF0
functions.evidence_summary: The Spirit Link buff's +0xF8 returns group 2; its +0xFC is therefore selected by the CUnit damage receiver's attached-object callback loop. The buff method inspects the incoming event and makes a virtual +0x364 call on an event-referenced object. Separately, the Spirit Link buff vtable's own +0x364 method (0x00C20AF0) enumerates SpiritLinkUnitData targets, initializes a secondary payload with mask 0x01000000, and dispatches it through each linked target's +0x120, temporarily setting and clearing target flag bit 0x100. This recovers a linked-unit damage redispatch path; the static event receiver identity at the +0xFC virtual call and the exact share fraction/data-field mapping remain unresolved.
functions.related_addresses_semantics: Addresses mentioned in the source evidence; not a verified caller/callee edge list.

functions.label: Damage group 5: +0xF8=0x00C7A3E0, +0xFC=0x00C7A3F0
functions.evidence_summary: The Mana Shield buff's +0xF8 returns group 5, routing its +0xFC method through the CUnit damage callback loop. The handler reads the incoming event amount (param2[4]) and buff floats at +0xD0, +0xD4, and +0xDC, updates its tracked values through numeric helpers, and calls 0x006D8530 to remove the buff when its depletion branches reach zero. It also calls 0x0069E310; that helper can emit mana-spend event 0xD02A0 when requested, but this callback passes its event flag as zero.
